{

      "id": "section_1",
      "title": "Sec 1: Prerequisite Warm-Up: Vectors on a Grid",
      "lecture_lines": [
        "2D vectors are arrows or coordinate pairs.",
        "Basis e1=(1,0), e2=(0,1) define the grid.",
        "Robot v=(2,1) is 2e1+1e2."
      ],
      "animations": [
        "Color lecture line 1 to #FFD166 only; on background #000000, fade in a light grid #2B2B2B with an origin dot #FFFFFF; draw a simple robot from circles and rectangles at (2,1) in #7AE582, label it 'robot' #7AE582; draw arrow from origin to robot in #FFD166 and label it 'v=(2,1)' #FFD166.",

        "Color lecture line 3 to #FFD166 only; show 2 units along e1 #4DD0E1 and 1 unit along e2 #FF6BCB, form the parallelogram, and draw resultant arrow to (2,1) #FFD166; place label '2e1+1e2=(2,1)' #FFD166 near the resultant."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "section_2",
      "title": "Sec 2: What Makes a Transformation Linear?",
      "lecture_lines": [
        "Linear T preserves addition: T(u+v)=T(u)+T(v).",
        "Linear T preserves scaling: T(cu)=cT(u).",
        "Origin stays fixed; grid lines stay straight.",
        "Parallel lines remain parallel; spacing stays even.",
        "Translation is not linear: it moves the origin."
      ],
      "animations": [
        "Color lecture line 1 to #FFD166 only; on grid #2B2B2B over #000000, draw u #4DD0E1, v #FF6BCB, and u+v #FFD166 as arrows from the origin; apply horizontal stretch T(x,y)=(2x,y) to the grid and arrows; label 'T(u+v)=T(u)+T(v)' #FFD166 and flash the matching endpoints.",
        "Color lecture line 2 to #FFD166 only; draw vector u #4DD0E1 and scaled vector cu #FF6BCB; apply T to both and show T(cu) coincides with cT(u); label 'T(cu)=cT(u)' #FFD166 and flash the matching arrow tips.",
        "Color lecture line 3 to #FFD166 only; show a square grid #2B2B2B under T(x,y)=(2x,y); mark the origin dot #FF5D5D with label 'origin fixed' #FF5D5D; animate several grid lines remaining straight, without numeric axes.",

        "Color lecture line 5 to #FFD166 only; animate a translation moving the grid and robot up-right so the origin dot #FF5D5D visibly leaves the origin; flash a red X with label 'translation: not linear' #FF5D5D; briefly bend one grid line #FF9F1C to reinforce nonlinearity."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "section_3",
      "title": "Sec 3: A Matrix Is a Transformation Recipe",
      "lecture_lines": [
        "A 2×2 matrix stores two column vectors.",
        "Column 1 is T(e1); column 2 is T(e2).",
        "Av=x(column 1)+y(column 2).",
        "Basis images determine every vector by linearity.",
        "A=[[2,0],[0,1]] stretches x-coordinates."
      ],
      "animations": [
        "Color lecture line 1 to #FFD166 only; reveal matrix A=[[a,b],[c,d]] in #FFFFFF on #000000; color column 1 #4DD0E1 and column 2 #FF6BCB; place labels 'col 1' #4DD0E1 and 'col 2' #FF6BCB directly beside the columns.",
        "Color lecture line 2 to #FFD166 only; draw e1 #4DD0E1 and e2 #FF6BCB on the grid; animate e1 moving to vector (a,c) labeled 'T(e1)=col1' #4DD0E1 and e2 moving to (b,d) labeled 'T(e2)=col2' #FF6BCB.",
        "Color lecture line 3 to #FFD166 only; show vector v=(x,y) #7AE582; draw x times column1 #4DD0E1 plus y times column2 #FF6BCB as arrows; label the resultant 'Av=x col1 + y col2' #FFD166.",

        "Color lecture line 5 to #FFD166 only; show A=[[2,0],[0,1]] #FFFFFF; map e1 #4DD0E1 to (2,0) and e2 #FF6BCB to (0,1); move robot from (2,1) #7AE582 to (4,1) #FFD166; label 'A(2,1)=(4,1)' #FFD166."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "section_4",
      "title": "Sec 4: Matrix–Vector Multiplication in Action",
      "lecture_lines": [
        "Matrix–vector product: multiply entries and add.",
        "Same product: weighted sum of columns.",
        "Color x times column 1; y times column 2.",
        "Rotation matrix A=[[0,-1],[1,0]] turns 90° CCW.",
        "A(2,1)=(-1,2) by algebra and columns."
      ],

        "Color lecture line 1 to #FFD166 only; display A=[[0,-1],[1,0]] #FFFFFF and v=(2,1) #7AE582; compute top row 0·2+(-1)·1=-1 #4DD0E1 and bottom row 1·2+0·1=2 #FF6BCB; label result 'Av=(-1,2)' #FFD166.",
        "Color lecture line 2 to #FFD166 only; show column1=(0,1) #4DD0E1 and column2=(-1,0) #FF6BCB; draw 2·column1 plus 1·column2 as arrows; label 'weighted column sum' #FFD166 near resultant (-1,2).",
        "Color lecture line 3 to #FFD166 only; color x=2 times column1 #4DD0E1 and y=1 times column2 #FF6BCB; add the scaled column arrows tip-to-tail to reach (-1,2) #FFD166; flash the two scaled pieces.",
        "Color lecture line 4 to #FFD166 only; draw vector (2,1) #7AE582 and rotate it 90° counterclockwise about the origin with an arc arrow #FFD166 to (-1,2) #FFD166; label 'rotation 90° CCW' #FFD166.",
        "Color lecture line 5 to #FFD166 only; place the algebraic calculation upper-left and the column construction on the grid without bordered panels; both resolve to point (-1,2) #FFD166; flash label 'same result' #7AE582."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "section_5",
      "title": "Sec 5: Gallery of Geometric Effects",
      "lecture_lines": [
        "Scaling doubles distance from the origin.",
        "Rotation turns 90°; shear slants the grid.",
        "Reflection flips across the x-axis."
      ],
      "animations": [
        "Color lecture line 1 to #FFD166 only; show the same primitive robot at (2,1) #7AE582 and matrix A=[[2,0],[0,2]] #4DD0E1; animate the robot and grid scaling to (4,2); label 'scaling: distance doubles' #4DD0E1.",
        "Color lecture line 2 to #FFD166 only; show rotation A=[[0,-1],[1,0]] #FF6BCB rotating the robot 90°, then shear A=[[1,1],[0,1]] #FF9F1C slanting the grid and robot; label 'rotation' #FF6BCB and 'shear' #FF9F1C.",
        "Color lecture line 3 to #FFD166 only; draw a faint horizontal x-axis #3A3A3A labeled 'x-axis' #E0E0E0 because reflection requires it; apply A=[[1,0],[0,-1]] #FF5D5D to flip the robot across the x-axis; label 'reflection' #FF5D5D."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "section_6",
      "title": "Sec 6: Recap and Mini Application",
      "lecture_lines": [
        "Linear maps preserve addition and scalar multiplication.",
        "A matrix records images of basis vectors.",
        "Av combines matrix columns; this animates graphics."
      ],
      "animations": [
        "Color lecture line 1 to #FFD166 only; replay small arrows u #4DD0E1, v #FF6BCB, u+v #FFD166, and scaled cu #7AE582; label 'preserve add + scale' #FFD166 near the arrows; flash matching endpoints.",
        "Color lecture line 2 to #FFD166 only; show e1 #4DD0E1 and e2 #FF6BCB moving to the matrix columns for A=[[0,-1],[1,0]] #FFFFFF; label 'basis images stored in A' #FFD166.",
        "Color lecture line 3 to #FFD166 only; build a robot from circles and rectangles #7AE582; apply A=[[0,-1],[1,0]] to every vertex, rotating hat, arm, and body together; map pointing v=(1,0) to (0,1) #FFD166, animate a small wave, and label 'avatar graphics use matrices' #7AE582."
      ]
    }
  ]
}
